B. <u>Solid Waste</u>: The agency believes that the additional use of 5.26 million pounds of plastics is likely to result in a minor increase in the solid waste disposal problem, particularly with respect to recycling.
At the present time, little of the additional plastics would be recycled. However, this may change as basic resources become less available and therefore more valuable. The degree to which recycling becomes available as a disposal technique is dependent upon political and economic factors and the availability of sanitary landfills, pyrolytic furnaces, and solid waste handling and sorting machinery. The automobile is considered a likely candidate for resource recovery because of the relatively high value of the materials and the fact that they can be brought to the site of the recovery facility in a unit. However, the variety of materials present in automobiles hampers the efforts to increase resource recovery.
